FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.98
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78
DESCRIPTION: `CorrelatedFailureModel` is declared with `@dataclass` but not instantiated correctly in `DynamicManager.__init__`. The fields `_vulnerabilities` and `_base_failure_rates` are dataclass `Field` objects because the class itself is missing the `@dataclass` decorator marker syntax before the class body in executable effect? More importantly, if instantiated as written with `CorrelatedFailureModel()`, correctness depends on dataclass transformation. If that transformation is absent or broken, methods like `self._vulnerabilities[key] = v_ij` fail immediately. This is a hard runtime break in the correlated failure subsystem.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Ensure `CorrelatedFailureModel` is actually decorated with `@dataclass` exactly as intended and add a smoke test that calls `set_vulnerability()` and `set_base_failure_rate()` on a fresh instance.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.93
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.84
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` emits the wrong event type for format violations. In the FORMAT branch it emits `ManagerEventType.MALFORMED` instead of `ManagerEventType.FORMAT_VIOLATION`. This makes downstream monitoring, alerting, and analytics misclassify protocol/format errors as parse failures, corrupting operational telemetry and any policy keyed to event type.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Change the FORMAT branch to emit `ManagerEventType.FORMAT_VIOLATION`. Add a test asserting that `format_compliant=False, parseable=True` produces `FailureType.FORMAT` and event type `FORMAT_VIOLATION`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.82
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` computes `mu` using `self.diminishing_returns.marginal_value(round_idx)` but the stop predicate uses smoothed/per-model-aware logic. The health monitor is then fed the unsmoothed system-level `mu`, not the effective stop signal. This creates an internal inconsistency: the system decides stopping with one metric family and diagnoses detector pathologies with another. That can trigger false “mu distortion” diagnoses or miss real ones.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Feed `DetectorHealthMonitor.record_round()` the same effective mu used for stopping, e.g. `smoothed_marginal_value(round_idx)` or `aggregate_per_model_mu(round_idx)` depending on design intent. Keep raw mu as separate metadata if needed.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.90
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76
DESCRIPTION: `DiminishingReturnsDetector.stop()` claims to implement an “ascending abstraction guard” and says the guard is conjunctive, but the implementation ignores `_abstraction_dropping()` entirely. The documented design decision is not present in the actual predicate. This is a spec/code divergence in a core stopping rule and can materially change termination behavior.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either incorporate `_abstraction_dropping(round_idx)` into `stop()` per the intended conjunctive rule, or remove the claim from docs/comments and dead helper if the guard was intentionally dropped.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73
DESCRIPTION: `RoundProgressionFSM.select_event()` can return `Event.COMPLETE` from `ROUND_{max_round_idx}` only after checking and converting it to `Event.MAX`, but from `SYNTH` it always returns `COMPLETE` even if `max_rounds=1`. That allows transition to `ROUND_1` although `max_rounds - 1 == 0`, exceeding the documented state budget. The FSM and `max_rounds` semantics are inconsistent for the smallest valid configuration.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Define whether `max_rounds` includes BLIND/SYNTH or only iterative rounds, then enforce it in both `valid_events()` and `transition()`. Add tests for `max_rounds=1` and `max_rounds=2`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F006
SEVERITY: 0.87
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManagementConfig.__post_init__()` validates only a subset of bounded parameters. Many values documented as probabilities/fractions/thresholds are unchecked: `epsilon_rho`, `lambda_lat`, `lambda_bal`, `epsilon_bal`, `tau_critical`, `tau_moderate`, `tau_mu`, `tau_novelty_stop`, `tau_novelty`, `epsilon_cost`, `timeout_multiplier`, `theta_under`, `eta_underperform`, `delta_deg`, `default_vulnerability`, `fingerprint_ema_alpha`, `fingerprint_min_signal`, and model baselines `b_*`. Invalid values can silently produce nonsense behavior.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add full invariant checks for all bounded/scalar parameters and all `b_*` vectors. Validate ordering constraints too, e.g. `tau_moderate <= tau_critical`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F007
SEVERITY: 0.86
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.get_ordering()` sorts only by stored capability score and not by the documented deterministic tie-break rule. When multiple models have equal scores, returned ordering is dependent on dict insertion order, which may not match assignment logic. Consumers relying on this ordering can observe inconsistency between `assign()` decisions and reported rankings.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Apply the same tie-break key used in `assign()` inside `get_ordering()`, using `_models` to recover fingerprints.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F008
SEVERITY: 0.84
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.reassign()` uses `len(self._models) >= 3` to decide whether to assign a COL, not the number of active models. If the run started with 3+ models but only 2 remain active, one active model is still labeled COL and the other PAR even though the earlier assignment logic treated COL as conditional on pool size. This creates inconsistent semantics under attrition.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Base COL eligibility on `len(active_models) >= 3` instead of initial pool size. Add tests for degradation from 3 models to 2 and 1.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F009
SEVERITY: 0.83
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer._redundancy_target()` uses total configured model count `K = len(self.models)` rather than admissible/active non-PM count for task coverage. For critical tasks with a PM excluded, the target may exceed the number of admissible assignees and become structurally unattainable. The solver then degrades silently.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Compute redundancy against the count of admissible active models for that task, or clamp target to admissible capacity. Emit an explicit diagnostic when requested redundancy is impossible.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F010
SEVERITY: 0.82
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.67
DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer._solve_greedy()` intentionally force-assigns a task when no feasible assignment satisfies F1, creating known HARD constraint violations while comments still describe respecting F1. This is a policy contradiction: the module claims to solve constrained allocation but can knowingly output infeasible solutions. Warning later is not equivalent to respecting HARD feasibility.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Separate “best-effort allocation” from “feasible allocation.” Either raise/return infeasible status without violating F1, or expose an explicit fallback mode that callers opt into.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F011
SEVERITY: 0.81
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.get_allocation()` returns `(allocation, cost, is_balanced)` but does not provide any infeasibility/violation information from `LoadBalancer.solve()`. Since the solver can knowingly violate HARD constraints and only emit warnings, the interface hides critical allocation validity from the orchestrator.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Extend the return type to include `feasible` and `violations`, or raise on infeasible allocations.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F012
SEVERITY: 0.80
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector._compute_equivalence_classes()` assigns `flaw_class = members[0].flaw_class` even though cross-class clustering is explicitly allowed when textual similarity is high. The resulting equivalence class then has an arbitrary representative flaw class, which can mislead downstream consumers and distort class-based reporting.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either forbid cross-class clustering, or represent class membership explicitly as a set / mixed label and handle it downstream.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F013
SEVERITY: 0.79
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.70
DESCRIPTION: The similarity relation used for convergence clustering is not transitive because it is thresholded pairwise similarity, but `_compute_equivalence_classes()` applies single-linkage union-find as if it were an equivalence relation. This can chain weakly related findings into one class even when endpoints are below threshold, inflating convergence and suppressing novelty.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either document and justify single-linkage as an approximation, or use complete-linkage / clique-based clustering if true equivalence behavior is required.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F014
SEVERITY: 0.77
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55
DESCRIPTION: `_tokenize_for_similarity()` uses plain whitespace splitting and does not strip punctuation. Tokens like `parser`, `parser.` and `parser)` are treated as different, weakening duplicate detection and convergence estimation.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Normalize punctuation with regex tokenization, possibly preserving identifiers separately for code-review text. Add tests with punctuation variants.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F015
SEVERITY: 0.76
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector.validate_no_findings()` docstring says “not converged unless null_expected,” but the validator only checks `kappa_set(2) == 1.0` and does not test `converged()`. The validator therefore does not validate the documented edge-case behavior.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Update the validator to assert the intended convergence behavior explicitly, or fix the docstring to match what is actually being validated.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F016
SEVERITY: 0.75
FLAW_CLASS: 8
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.49
DESCRIPTION: `FailureType` docstring says lower enum value means higher priority, but actual detection priority is encoded procedurally in `detect_failure()`, not via enum ordering. This documentation invites misuse by future code that sorts by enum value assuming it controls behavior.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Clarify that enum numeric values are descriptive only, or centralize priority in a single ordering table used by detection logic and docs.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F017
SEVERITY: 0.74
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.get_recovery()` counts repeats with `same_type_count >= n_fail` before recording the current failure. With default `n_fail=2`, escalation occurs on the third occurrence, not the second. The inline validator comments acknowledge this, meaning the parameter semantics are off by one relative to likely reader expectation of “failure repetition threshold.”  
PROPOSED_FIX: Define `n_fail` semantics clearly as “prior failures before escalation” or change logic to `same_type_count + 1 >= n_fail`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F018
SEVERITY: 0.73
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.59
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.get_recovery()` determines actions but emits no recovery events (`RETRY`, `EXCLUDE`, `ABORT`, etc.) through the event callback, despite those event types existing in `ManagerEventType`. The monitoring interface is therefore incomplete: it reports failure detection but not recovery decisions.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Emit corresponding recovery events in `get_recovery()` after action selection and state mutation.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F019
SEVERITY: 0.72
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.68
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` emits events for EMPTY/TIMEOUT/MALFORMED/FORMAT but not for UNDERPERFORM, even though `ManagerEventType.UNDERPERFORM` exists. This leaves a blind spot in real-time manager monitoring for one of the defined failure types.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Emit `ManagerEventType.UNDERPERFORM` when the persistence condition is met.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F020
SEVERITY: 0.71
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.should_abort()` comments say “If only PM survives, framework degrades to single-model mode,” but the logic only checks `len(active_models) < k_min` and PM presence. If `k_min` is configured >1, surviving PM-only state aborts despite the comment. The behavior is config-dependent but undocumented in the condition.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either codify PM-only degradation irrespective of `k_min`, or revise docs/comments to say degradation occurs only when consistent with `k_min`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F021
SEVERITY: 0.70
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` updates live fingerprints only when not terminal. That discards the final round’s observational data, even though the final round may contain the most informative failure/convergence evidence and could be needed for post-run diagnostics or training.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Update fingerprints unconditionally after processing the round, or store final-round observations separately if allocation reuse is the reason for skipping.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F022
SEVERITY: 0.69
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` computes per-model costs only for `active` models after failure handling. A model that responded this round but is excluded due to that same round’s failure may be omitted from cost attribution, distorting per-model mu and health diagnostics.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Attribute round cost across responding/dispatched models for that round, not post-failure active set.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F023
SEVERITY: 0.68
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.54
DESCRIPTION: In per-model cost attribution, a missing response for an active model contributes zero content length, which can shift nearly all cost onto verbose responders even if silence itself consumed dispatch resources. This biases `per_model_mu` in favor of failed or terse models.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Base cost on dispatched allocation or a hybrid of fixed per-dispatch cost plus variable output-size cost.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F024
SEVERITY: 0.67
FLAW_CLASS: 7
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.46
DESCRIPTION: `Allocation.get_assigned_models()`, `get_assigned_tasks()`, and `model_load()` use repeated linear searches via `.index()` and task-map reconstruction. On repeated calls this becomes avoidable overhead.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Precompute index maps and/or task lookup dictionaries inside `Allocation`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F025
SEVERITY: 0.67
FLAW_CLASS: 7
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.reassign()` does repeated linear search `next((m for m in models_for_scoring ...))` for each active model. This is O(K^2) and unnecessary since model IDs are unique and stable.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Build a `model_by_id` dict once per reassignment.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F026
SEVERITY: 0.66
FLAW_CLASS: 7
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector._compute_equivalence_classes()` is O(n^2) pairwise similarity with tokenization repeated per pair. For large finding sets, this is expensive and scales poorly.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Cache tokenized forms per finding and consider blocking by flaw class / lexical signatures before pairwise comparison.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F027
SEVERITY: 0.65
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: `_finding_similarity()` returns a hardcoded 0.8 for two empty descriptions with matching flaw class. Since default `tau_sim` is also 0.8, any two same-class empty-description findings collapse as duplicates automatically. That can spuriously inflate convergence when models omit descriptions.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Lower the empty-text similarity, require additional fields for equivalence, or treat empty descriptions as insufficient evidence for merging.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F028
SEVERITY: 0.64
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.52
DESCRIPTION: `CapabilityFingerprint.as_normalised_array()` can produce negative first component if a model’s `D_decay` exceeds `pool_max` due to inconsistent input or NaN propagation, and no fingerprint field validation exists. Similar issues apply to other dimensions exceeding expected ranges.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate `CapabilityFingerprint` values on construction and clamp/raise on invalid normalization inputs.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F029
SEVERITY: 0.63
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.60
DESCRIPTION: `ModelSpec`, `Task`, `Finding`, and `ModelResponse` accept obviously invalid values such as negative times, negative token demand, severity outside [0,1], or abstraction outside [0,1]. Since these are core domain types, invalid instances can poison multiple subsystems before failure surfaces.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add `__post_init__` validation to these dataclasses for documented invariants.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F030
SEVERITY: 0.62
FLAW_CLASS: 8
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.43
DESCRIPTION: The top-level module docstring claims “All six areas ... are implemented,” but the file also contains a seventh “Detector Health Monitor” area plus registry/immune/dispatch extensions. The artifact boundary is unclear and the summary is stale.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Update module documentation to reflect actual implemented areas and extensions.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F031
SEVERITY: 0.61
FLAW_CLASS: 8
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.44
DESCRIPTION: Several comments refer to prior findings, experiments, and external models as if they are normative proofs, but no executable tests tie those claims to behavior. This weakens maintainability because future readers cannot distinguish justified constraints from historical commentary.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Convert critical experiment-derived fixes into regression tests and reduce narrative comments to concise rationale.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F032
SEVERITY: 0.60
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66
DESCRIPTION: `DetectorHealthMonitor` adaptive sensitivity comments say repeated exposure “narrows the window and speeds response,” but implementation widens the effective window with each resolved pathology and does nothing with persistent pathology except severity escalation. The formal commentary and code disagree.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either implement the stated adaptive law or rewrite the comments to match actual behavior.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F033
SEVERITY: 0.59
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.56
DESCRIPTION: `DetectorHealthMonitor.record_round()` increments `_pathology_counts["kappa"]` when kappa is stuck, but the analogous mu pathology branch never increments `_pathology_counts["mu"]`. The later “resolved” logic for mu therefore cannot function as intended.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Increment `_pathology_counts["mu"]` when the mu pathology is detected, mirroring kappa.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F034
SEVERITY: 0.58
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57
DESCRIPTION: `effective_window()` computes `persistent = self._pathology_counts.get(detector, 0)` but never uses it. This is dead logic in a core adaptive-monitoring mechanism and suggests the implementation is incomplete.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Remove the unused variable or use it to adjust sensitivity/severity per the intended design.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F035
SEVERITY: 0.57
FLAW_CLASS: 7
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` imports `defaultdict` inside the method twice. This is minor but unnecessary overhead and noise in a hot orchestration path.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Move imports to module scope.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F036
SEVERITY: 0.56
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.53
DESCRIPTION: `RoundResult.allocation` is always set to `None` with a comment “Caller retains allocation reference.” This means the main orchestration result object is missing a key cross-area artifact despite claiming to capture all outputs needed for communication.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Accept allocation as an optional `process_round()` argument and persist it in `RoundResult`, or remove the field if intentionally external.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F037
SEVERITY: 0.55
FLAW_CLASS: 8
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.40
DESCRIPTION: `State.round_state()` docstring says “Return the state name for ROUND_k,” but returned values are plain strings, while `State` otherwise uses enum values. This blurs the type model and contributes to stringly-typed FSM state handling.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either make all FSM states string-based consistently in docs/types, or represent round states as structured values rather than strings.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F038
SEVERITY: 0.54
FLAW_CLASS: 3
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.38
DESCRIPTION: The artifact mixes mathematical notation in comments with Python identifiers inconsistently, e.g. `k_total` in admissibility is not actually total K, `Delta_r` becomes `adoption_delta`, and “class” is overloaded between flaw class and equivalence class. This increases cognitive load and invites specification drift.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add a compact notation-to-code mapping table and rename the most misleading locals.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F039
SEVERITY: 0.53
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47
DESCRIPTION: `ManagerEventStream.drain()` returns the underlying buffer list object before replacing it. If external code mutates that list, prior references remain mutable and can confuse downstream consumers.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Return a copy via `list(self._buffer)` before clearing.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F040
SEVERITY: 0.52
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.51
DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer._objective()` treats zero/negative limits as fraction 0.0 under `np.where(limits > 0, loads / limits, 0.0)`. A model with invalid nonpositive capacity can therefore look cost-free in latency and balance terms even while impossible to use.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Treat nonpositive limit with positive load as `inf` fraction, matching `Allocation.model_load_fraction()`, and validate `L > 0` in `ModelSpec`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F041
SEVERITY: 0.51
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.50
DESCRIPTION: `feasibility_probability()` uses a normal approximation for uncertain token limit without guarding against negative sampled capacities or pathological `L_std >> L`. The resulting probability may be mathematically valid but operationally badly calibrated for bounded capacities.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Document this as a heuristic and consider truncated-normal or lognormal modeling for strictly nonnegative capacities.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F042
SEVERITY: 0.50
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55
DESCRIPTION: The correlated failure subsystem is not integrated into any dispatch, allocation, or stopping decision. It exists as an isolated utility plus smoke test, so the claimed “Area 6 extension” is incomplete at system level.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Incorporate independence/correlation penalties into redundancy planning or risk diagnostics, or downgrade the claim from implemented extension to utility available for integration.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
